title: Multilingual Machine Translation with Open Large Language Models at Practical Scale: An Empirical Study

live_model.evidence: "GPT-3.5/4 Turbo: The translation performance by leveraging the OpenAI API4 with greedy decoding for inference" (Sec. 3.2); Table 1 row GPT-4-turbo, FLORES-200 en→xx column 37.01/87.14 (spBLEU/COMET)

prompt.location: Sec. 3.2 (in-context template format "<X>=<Y>"), Sec. 4.2, Appendix Table 4 (per-language results)
prompt.note: 5 randomly selected FLORES-200 dev sentence pairs used as in-context exemplars per direction; exact exemplar sentences and any system/instruction text are not printed, only the template format.

claim.metric: spBLEU, FLORES-200 en->xx (5-shot in-context, greedy decoding)
claim.location: Table 1, row GPT-4-turbo, FLORES-200 en→xx column (spBLEU/COMET); 1012 sentences x 27 non-English target languages (Table 3 lists all 28 languages, Appendix Table 4 gives the per-language breakdown)

data.source: FLORES-200 devtest (Meta/NLLB) and WMT-24 test sets

notes: NAACL 2025. Baselines (GPT-3.5/4 Turbo, Google Translate) are run by the authors via the OpenAI API with the same 5-shot in-context strategy as the open models; per-language cells in Appendix Table 4/5/6 let a scorer pick a cheaper single-language slice if full 28-language reproduction is too costly.
